correctness.rationale: For \(0<\lambda<1\) and \(0<a<1\), the symbol is entire and belongs to Gaussian Fock space. Exact cancellation \(M(z)=|g_a(z)|e^{-\beta(\operatorname{Im}z)^2}\), together with uniform Riemann--Lebesgue decay, proves \(M\in C_0(\mathbb C)\); the change-of-variable norm estimate and locally compact restriction establish operator compactness. Du (2011) gives the bounded-operator \(S_p\) criterion, which applies to \(\phi(z)=\lambda z\). The Gaussian-dominated Fourier-edge asymptotic reduces its integral to \(\int_1^\infty x^{-p(1-a)}dx\), convergent exactly when \(p>1/(1-a)\). Direct basis summation and Plancherel prove the exact Hilbert--Schmidt formula, while dominated convergence of the Fourier leading term gives the horizontal-window constants. Endpoints \(p=1/(1-a)\) and \(a=1/2\), and normalization \(1/\pi\), are handled. No finite experiment substitutes for an infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The construction answers a published 2026 compactness-implies-Hilbert--Schmidt question negatively already at its Gaussian member, and gives a complete sharp Schatten-ideal membership threshold for a natural singular-Fourier parameter family. The exact logarithmic-versus-power transition quantifies the mechanism, beyond a yes/no counterexample. This is motivated, nontrivial finite analytic structure; the general 2011 criterion is acknowledged and the additional entire construction and sharp estimates are essential.
